sections.heading: Pull request — exfer-stack/exfer-indexer #1 (closed)
sections.text:
feat(follower): index input-side (outgoing) address activity
In exfer-stack/exfer-indexer, his own repository.
https://github.com/exfer-stack/exfer-indexer/pull/1

## Problem

The follower only wrote **output-side** rows into `tx_by_address` (`is_input: false`),
so `get_address_history` returned *received* funds but never *sent* funds — despite
the module's header comment promising "a row per output recipient, **every input
spender**". Every outgoing transfer was invisible to address-history consumers
(notably the mobile wallet's Activity feed, which classifies sends from
`direction:"input"`).

## Fix

In `process_block`, for each non-coinbase input, resolve the previous output (its
32-byte P2PKH locking script = the address, plus its value) by fetching the prev tx
from the node — cached per block since several inputs can share a prevout — and emit
`AddressActivity{ is_input: true }`. Covenant/HTLC prevouts (non-32-byte scripts) are
skipped, mirroring the output-side rule. Transport errors propagate so the block
retries; a genuinely-absent prevout is skipped rather than wedging the follower.

## Tests

Storage + query already round-trip both directions
(`get_address_history_returns_activity_rows` asserts `"output"` and `"input"`); this
fills the producer side. `cargo test` green (30 tests); validated live by re-indexing
the deployed node and confirming a real `direction:"input"` row.
